text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian envoys attending a Council of Europe conference in Brussels refused a proposal from Turkey calling for Bosnia's acceptance in the European organisation. Moslem-Croat federation prime minister Edhem Bicakcic says such a decision would be premature and counter-productive.
- Bosnian Serb representatives did not attend the Council of Europe conference because they declined to carry Bosnian passports and were refused visas, diplomatic sources say.

- Planned negotiations on Thursday in London between Bosnia-Herzegovina and the London Club of creditors should result in rescheduling of the country's debt, creating conditions for new loans and rapid reconstruction.

- Under a draft law before Bosnia's Serb national assembly regulating the sale of flats, those who do not currently live in an apartment are barred from purchasing it. The newspaper says the adoption of the draft law would effectively complete the process of wartime "ethnic cleansing".

- The opposition Social Democratic Party said it opposes dividing municipalities along national lines and accuses the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) of obstructing the work of the federation parliament over the issue.
- Ministry of foreign affairs says Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic scheduled meetings with British diplomats in London without consulting the ministry.

- The new High Representative to Bosnia, Carlos Westendorp, said in Brussels that his three main priorities are democratisation, economic recovery and establishment of a working political system in the country. --Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
